name: statsgrokse
what_it_holds: R binding (GPL>=2, last release 2017-03-22) to the now-defunct stats.grok.se pageview mirror, covering Wikipedia pageview counts 2008-2015 (the pre-official-API era) by article/language/date range.
why_useful: The only tool found in this sweep that reaches PRE-2015 Wikipedia pageview history, which is otherwise unavailable from the official API/dumps. Low relevance to ABNB itself (founded 2008, IPO 2020) but could extend a destination-interest panel a few years further back than any other pageviews source, or serve pre-2015 case studies of other travel/kernel businesses.
time_coverage: 2008-2015 (fills the gap before official Wikimedia pageviews dumps begin)
size_hint: small R package, no bundled data
themes: Wikipedia pageviews tooling and destination-demand datasets (pageviews for cities/attractions as tourism proxies)
why_all: The only tool found in this sweep that reaches PRE-2015 Wikipedia pageview history, which is otherwise unavailable from the official API/dumps. Low relevance to ABNB itself (founded 2008, IPO 2020) but could extend a destination-interest panel a few years further back than any other pageviews source, or serve pre-2015 case studies of other travel/kernel businesses.

Companion/underlying tool to wikipediatrend's historical stitch; useful if that package's hosted historical mirror ever goes down, since it hits the original stats.grok.se archive directly for 2008-2015 city/destination article views.

name: kaggle-web-traffic (1st place solution, Wikipedia Web Traffic Forecasting)
what_it_holds: 1st-place solution code (MIT license) for Google/Kaggle's 'Web Traffic Time Series Forecasting' competition, which itself is built on a public dataset of ~145,000 Wikipedia articles' daily pageviews (train_2.csv/key_2.csv, roughly Jul 2015-Sep 2017, multiple languages including many city/country/landmark/tourism-related articles). Data must be pulled from Kaggle (kaggle.com/c/web-traffic-time-series-forecasting) rather than the repo itself; repo only has the RNN encoder-decoder modeling code.
why_useful: The underlying Kaggle dataset (pointer, not in this repo) is a large, ready-made multi-year daily pageview panel across ~145k Wikipedia articles in several languages, which almost certainly includes major tourist-destination cities/landmarks/countries as dense daily series 2015-2017 - useful as a historical validation set for 'does city pageview level/growth lead STR/hotel demand' even though it predates the Airbnb-relevant recent quarters. Also a source of mixed-frequency/time-series forecasting method ideas (Gap 17).
geography: global, multi-language Wikipedia (city/country/landmark articles included among the ~145k)
size_hint: 145,000 time series x ~800 days; dataset lives on Kaggle, repo is code-only
license: MIT (code); Kaggle competition data terms apply to the dataset itself
themes: Wikipedia pageviews tooling and destination-demand datasets (pageviews for cities/attractions as tourism proxies)
why_all: The underlying Kaggle dataset (pointer, not in this repo) is a large, ready-made multi-year daily pageview panel across ~145k Wikipedia articles in several languages, which almost certainly includes major tourist-destination cities/landmarks/countries as dense daily series 2015-2017 - useful as a historical validation set for 'does city pageview level/growth lead STR/hotel demand' even though it predates the Airbnb-relevant recent quarters. Also a source of mixed-frequency/time-series forecasting method ideas (Gap 17).

name: cloudflare-radar-rankings-cache
what_it_holds: Automated daily/weekly mirror of Cloudflare Radar's domain popularity rankings, committed as gzip-compressed CSVs at four tiers (top-1k, top-10k, top-100k, top-1m), one 'domain' column per file, unordered (membership-only, not rank-ordered). Stored both as dated snapshots (YYYY-MM-DD dirs, so a time series builds up) and a current/ pointer. MIT-licensed code, data itself under Cloudflare Radar terms. Actively updated (commit within the last day as of scrape).
why_useful: Gives a longitudinal, point-in-time-able snapshot of which domains are in Cloudflare's top-N popularity tiers each day/week — the closest free proxy to a Similarweb-style traffic-rank history for airbnb.com and competitor domains (booking.com, vrbo.com, expedia.com). Speaks to gap 5 (engagement/web-traffic estimates) and could be checked for airbnb.com's tier membership over time as a crude traffic-trend indicator, with the caveat that it's membership not rank-value.
time_coverage: ongoing snapshots, apparently started 2026; check earliest commit for history depth
size_hint: 4 gzip CSVs per snapshot day, up to 1M rows in the largest tier
themes: Search/SEO and referral data: Bing/Google keyword volume tools, SERP scrapers, Common Crawl web graph, backlink datasets, AI-bot crawler traffic stats (Cloudflare, Vercel)
why_all: Gives a longitudinal, point-in-time-able snapshot of which domains are in Cloudflare's top-N popularity tiers each day/week — the closest free proxy to a Similarweb-style traffic-rank history for airbnb.com and competitor domains (booking.com, vrbo.com, expedia.com). Speaks to gap 5 (engagement/web-traffic estimates) and could be checked for airbnb.com's tier membership over time as a crude traffic-trend indicator, with the caveat that it's membership not rank-value.

name: cloudflare-bot-directory
what_it_holds: Single committed JSON file (src/index.json) listing 500+ verified crawlers/bots from Cloudflare Radar's Verified Bots directory, with fields slug, name, kind, operator, operatorUrl, category, description, followsRobotsTxt, userAgentPatterns, userAgents. This is a static snapshot, not a traffic-share time series.
why_useful: Directly on-theme for gap 19 (AI-referral traffic / bot crawler share) as a reference table of which bots exist and how to identify them in logs, but it holds no traffic volume or share data itself — only bot identity metadata. Useful mainly as a lookup table if we ever get log-level crawler-traffic data from elsewhere.
license: CC BY-NC 4.0 (data), repo code license unspecified
themes: Search/SEO and referral data: Bing/Google keyword volume tools, SERP scrapers, Common Crawl web graph, backlink datasets, AI-bot crawler traffic stats (Cloudflare, Vercel)
wildcard: a hedge-fund alternative-data buyer who has seen every vendo
wildcard: a quant building a KPI nowcast for a consumer-internet compa
why_all: Directly on-theme for gap 19 (AI-referral traffic / bot crawler share) as a reference table of which bots exist and how to identify them in logs, but it holds no traffic volume or share data itself — only bot identity metadata. Useful mainly as a lookup table if we ever get log-level crawler-traffic data from elsewhere.

Matches CONTEXT gap #19 ('AI-referral traffic: bot/crawler share datasets') directly — a maintained, structured list of bot UAs is the building block for classifying web-log or CDN traffic into AI-agent vs. human vs. search-engine share, relevant to how Airbnb's own site traffic mix may be shifting toward AI-agent referrals/bookings.

CONTEXT gap #19 (AI-referral traffic / bot-crawler share) names Cloudflare Radar directly; this is a maintained, machine-readable snapshot of the bot taxonomy Radar tracks, useful as a reference table for classifying AI-agent vs human traffic in any web-log or Common Crawl work the team already has (the Common Crawl CDX index over airbnb.com), though it is not itself a time series of bot traffic share.

name: cc-crawl-statistics
what_it_holds: Scripts (crawlstats.py, crawlplot.py) plus PUBLISHED per-crawl statistics (aggregated ~1MiB files + plots at commoncrawl.github.io/cc-crawl-statistics/) covering every monthly crawl from CC-MAIN-2008-2009 to present: page/URL/document counts by host, domain, TLD, MIME type, protocol (HTTP vs HTTPS share), and content language (since mid-2018). Apache-2.0, 317 commits.
why_useful: Could give a crude 'share of web indexed' time series by host, potentially proxying travel-site web presence/engagement trend over years, complementing our existing CDX/WARC captures.
size_hint: code only; pre-computed stats on S3 are modest CSVs per crawl
themes: Search/SEO and referral data: Bing/Google keyword volume tools, SERP scrapers, Common Crawl web graph, backlink datasets, AI-bot crawler traffic stats (Cloudflare, Vercel)
Common Crawl tooling: cdx-toolkit, warcio, host-level indexes, columnar index queries; datasets derived from Common Crawl for travel sites
why_all: Could give a crude 'share of web indexed' time series by host, potentially proxying travel-site web presence/engagement trend over years, complementing our existing CDX/WARC captures.

Gives a long, free, point-in-time-stamped (one file per monthly crawl, never revised) time series of overall web-crawl composition -- e.g., domain counts, HTTPS adoption, language mix -- useful as a macro internet-activity control variable, and the published files are themselves already a historical vintage register (each crawl's stats file is dated and never overwritten), which is exactly the kind of point-in-time discipline gap 4 wants, even though the subject is the whole web rather than ABNB-specific.
